cover.text: Google's CC started as a personal assistant. Now it runs the whole household.

slides.headline: Demand drove the pivot
slides.body: Tom Shane, senior product manager at Google Labs, wrote that "one of our top user requests was for CC to do more to help run a busy home." Household coordination across multiple accounts was the trigger.
slides.highlight: one of our top user requests

slides.headline: Who can join
slides.note: U.S. adults with personal Gmail only

slides.headline: Three ways to share with CC
slides.body: Forward a one-off email or photo. Set up auto-sharing from specific senders like a school or sports club. Or link a Drive folder or calendar directly.
slides.highlight: Forward a one-off email or photo

slides.headline: The daily briefing CC sends
slides.body: Every morning, CC sends "Your Day Ahead", who needs to be where, what tasks are pending, and what CC completed yesterday. It updates a shared family calendar and task list.

slides.headline: What CC can do on its own
slides.body: Pre-fill permission slips and activity registration forms, build school supply lists, draft meal plans, check live drive times between activities, create shared docs and sheets.

slides.headline: One catch: kids are locked out
slides.body: The experiment requires U.S. adults with personal Gmail accounts. Tweens, teens, and school-provided accounts are not eligible.

slides.headline: How to get it
slides.body: Existing CC users will get an email invitation to upgrade in the coming days. New users can join a waitlist.

follow: Follow Helios for coverage of AI agents moving from personal tools into shared, everyday life.
